name: B200 (Blackwell, GB200 NVL72 variant)
notes: Same 'Blackwell' silicon as b200-sxm-hgx.json, but binned to a higher power/thermal envelope (1200W vs 1000W) when deployed in the liquid-cooled GB200 NVL72 rack, yielding higher memory capacity (186GB vs 180GB), bandwidth (8 vs 7.7 TB/s), and compute across every Tensor Core precision. Per the official NVIDIA Blackwell datasheet's footnote 1, all Tensor Core figures except FP64 are shown as sparse-only (no dense value independently published) -- dense fields left null. FP8 and FP6 Tensor Core published as a single combined figure -- both fields carry the same source value. c2c_bandwidth_gbps of 900 GB/s (aggregate bidirectional NVLink-C2C to the Grace CPU) is documented at the GB200 Grace Blackwell Superchip level (1 Grace : 2 GPUs) in this datasheet's 'Decompression Engine' sidebar text, not stated as an explicit per-GPU figure -- recorded here as the superchip-level aggregate since the schema has no separate superchip tier.

_sources.c2c_bandwidth_gbps: https://www.primeline-solutions.com/media/categories/server/nach-gpu/nvidia-hgx-h200/nvidia-blackwell-b200-datasheet.pdf (p.8, Decompression Engine sidebar: '900 gigabytes per second (GB/s) of bidirectional bandwidth' to Grace CPU)
